sources.prompt:
Create ONE polished widescreen 16:9 concept image of a 2D hand-painted WUXIA turn-based battle game, specifically the IDLE STANDOFF camera view. This is a game composition mockup, not a movie poster and not a side-scroller. CAMERA: fixed behind the PLAYER, slightly offset to the player's left, around upper-back height, looking forward over his back toward the ENEMY. The player is in the lower-left foreground with his BACK and back-three-quarter shoulders clearly visible, head turned away looking at the enemy. Show entire player from head to grounded boots, occupying about 55 percent of image height; do NOT turn player face toward viewer. Opponent in upper-middle/right midground facing the player and camera, full body, about 35 percent image height, across a clearly visible 4-metre empty fighting gap. Both are poised, planted feet, lowered centres of gravity, subtle bent knees, relaxed but alert weapon-ready stances, no attacks underway. Their posture communicates quiet tense confrontation, NOT a crossed-blade impact or a running attack.
PLAYER: original Chinese wandering swordsman, adult male, long black hair tied in a high ponytail with dark jade ribbon, off-white linen inner garment, dark desaturated teal/ink-blue flowing outer robe with split hem, worn leather belt, small cinnabar red tassel, restrained bronze clasp. His right hand visibly wraps the dark handle of a long STRAIGHT Chinese jian sword, slim pale steel double-edged blade, modest bronze crossguard; blade held low diagonally toward the enemy, clearly connected to fist and wrist. No katana, no sci-fi or European armour. ENEMY: original masked swordsman in muted russet/brown layered travelling robes, charcoal sash, broad-brim woven bamboo hat, holds a slightly broader Chinese single-edged dao at the ready, facing player. Never show gore or injury.
ARENA: rain-darkened ancient stone courtyard on a mountain pass, shallow reflective puddles and scattered leaves, ruined timber pavilion right, mossy stone balustrade left, misty jade mountains and warm pale sky in background. Perspective stone seams define ground depth and both characters firmly stand on the SAME ground plane. Keep centre fighting space uncluttered and both weapon silhouettes easy to read.
VISUAL STYLE: premium coherent 2D painted GAME art, refined Chinese ink-and-colour illustration with crisp character contours, delicate cel-shaded cloth and metallic edge highlights, subtle brush-grain in distant mountains. This is COLOURED INK, NOT black-and-white: jade green/teal scenery, ink blue player, russet opponent, restrained cinnabar red and warm antique gold highlights, natural skin and steel colours. Small wisps of pale jade and ink-blue brushstroke qi near weapons only, very low intensity because IDLE, no large slash trails, no explosions, no floating shield. Colour and material remain legible, calm atmospheric tension, believable anatomy and naturally held weapons. Reserve calm upper sky and lower-right ground for potential future UI, but draw NO HUD, no health bars, no text, no lettering, no watermark, no borders, no collage. Single uninterrupted battle camera image.

sources.rejection_reason: Visual inspection found an extra player sword and cropped foreground boots. Kept for generation provenance, not included in the review board or production assets.
sources.prompt:
Create ONE polished widescreen 16:9 illustration of the WEAPON PARRY moment in an original 2D hand-painted WUXIA turn-based battle game. It must read as the same arena and behind-player battle camera as the idle setup described here. This is a game camera concept, not a movie poster, not a side-scroller, not a collage. No text, no UI, no labels or watermarks.
CAMERA: look from behind the PLAYER, slightly offset to his LEFT at upper-back height, toward the ENEMY. Player in lower-left foreground, BACK and rear-three-quarter shoulders visible, face looking AWAY toward opponent; entire head to firmly grounded boots visible. Enemy in middle-right facing toward player and camera, has stepped forward from idle to attack. Keep both characters FULL BODY, clear ground depth, no cropped weapons or limbs.
PLAYER: adult male wandering swordsman, long BLACK high ponytail tied with dark jade ribbon, OFF-WHITE linen sleeves and inner robe, dark desaturated TEAL/INK-BLUE sleeveless split-hem outer robe, brown leather waistbelt and bracers, small CINNABAR red tassel, brown boots. NOT silver hair, not a red-haired fantasy knight, not Western armour. His RIGHT hand visibly grips a dark wrapped hilt, bronze guard, long STRAIGHT Chinese double-edged JIAN with pale steel blade. Left hand supports right wrist or lower hilt naturally, no extra fingers. His knees sink, front boot plants, torso rotates slightly toward attack; he raises and angles his actual JIAN diagonally across the front of his shoulders to intercept an incoming blade. Hands and wrist mechanically support the blocking weapon. There is NO magic shield, no bubble, no floating defensive wall.
ENEMY: original swordsman in muted RUSSET/BROWN layered travelling robes, black sash, wide woven BAMBOO hat, face shadowed by hat. His right hand holds a broad curved Chinese DAO sword by its dark hilt; he makes a grounded forward cutting step toward player. No injury or gore.
MOST IMPORTANT: draw EXACTLY TWO complete held swords, each physically connected from its owner's wrapped fist through hilt/guard to blade tip. The player JIAN and enemy DAO visibly CROSS AND TOUCH near screen centre between their upper bodies. A SMALL local metallic contact point at the true crossing shows the successful block; swords resist each other, player does not block empty air. No third sword, no detached blade, no blades passing through torso. Both body silhouettes, hands and crossing weapons remain readable.
FX STYLE: refined COLOURED CHINESE INK, not black-and-white. At the blade-to-blade contact, a tiny warm ANTIQUE GOLD/ivory flash and 5-8 short gold sparks. Around that contact ONLY, one compact pale JADE/CYAN ink-brush crescent and several dark ink-blue broken brush fibres/small droplets, tapering with rough calligraphic edges. Keep the FX under 15 percent of the frame, leave weapon crossing clearly visible. Sense of crisp resisted force through grounded posture and short ink streaks, not a giant explosion or neon laser arc. No blood, no title calligraphy, no abstract poster.
ARENA: rain-darkened grey stone courtyard on a mountain pass; shallow puddle reflections, mossy stone balustrade along LEFT, old timber pavilion at RIGHT, misty JADE/TEAL mountains behind, warm pale parchment sky. Perspective paving lines, natural brown stone and timber colours. Same consistent premium 2D coloured ink/cel-painted art throughout: crisp dark character outlines, controlled cloth folds, metallic edges, softer ink mountain silhouettes. Restrained jade green/ink blue/russet/cinnabar and antique gold palette, natural skin and material colour. Clean cinematic battle composition where camera is clearly BEHIND the teal player facing the straw-hat opponent.

ONE full widescreen 16:9 2D hand-painted WUXIA GAME battle screenshot concept: successful sword BLOCK from a BEHIND-PLAYER camera. EXACTLY TWO PEOPLE and EXACTLY TWO SWORDS TOTAL, one sword per person. NO EXTRA SWORD, no sword at player's waist, no second sword in left hand, no sheathed blade sticking out. Every person's boots and full weapon tip fit inside image with generous bottom margin.
Fixed battle camera behind and slightly left of a foreground Chinese swordsman, viewing his BACK, not his face. Foreground player at lower LEFT is full body: black high ponytail tied with jade-green ribbon, dark TEAL sleeveless long split robe, CREAM long sleeves and pants, brown leather belt/bracers/boots, a single red tassel. He bends knees and firmly plants both feet. His RIGHT ARM IS RAISED at shoulder level: his RIGHT HAND firmly grips the only STRAIGHT SILVER JIAN SWORD by its dark handle and bronze guard. The jian extends DIAGONALLY UP-RIGHT across his front, tip toward upper right. His LEFT HAND IS EMPTY, pulled back beside left hip, clearly NOT HOLDING ANY WEAPON. No sword or sword tip near the player's knees. There is only one jian in the entire player's silhouette. Pose expresses braced resistance through back and shoulders, not idle with weapon still down.
Midground ENEMY at middle RIGHT facing the player: adult swordsman in RUSSET BROWN robe, black sash, woven broad BAMBOO HAT, dark boots. His RIGHT HAND holds his only CURVED DAO sword, chopping diagonally DOWN-LEFT toward player. The two blade lines form ONE clear X near CENTRE image: player's straight blade rising up-right, enemy's curved blade descending down-left. Both handles and guards are separate, connected correctly to their owner's right fists. The actual blades visibly meet at the X, neither enters anybody's torso. No blood or injuries. No magical defensive shield.
At the exact blade CROSSING, tiny IVORY/GOLD contact flash with a few short warm gold sparks, surrounded by a restrained thin JADE/CYAN INK-BRUSH stroke and small ink-blue flecks. Only a compact effect, no enormous arc, no explosion, no lightning. The steel crossing stays readable through effect. This is coloured ink-brush qi and metallic parry, not black-white abstract painting.
Same arena: grey rain-wet stone courtyard, small puddles and perspective stone seams, mossy stone railing on LEFT, old timber pavilion on RIGHT, misty JADE mountains and warm pale sky behind. Refined 2D painted art, crisp dark contours on character, controlled cloth folds and colour blocks, softer ink-watercolour background. Palette jade/teal/ink blue, cream, russet brown, small cinnabar red and antique gold accents. Strong spatial depth from near player's back to opponent facing camera. NOT 3D photoreal, not side scrolling, not poster. No text, HUD, calligraphy, watermark or panel borders. Single uninterrupted battle view. Prioritise anatomically correct ONE weapon in each person's RIGHT hand and an unambiguous TWO-BLADE CROSS at centre.

processing: Selected source PNGs copied without changing the art. Board aligns the two actual-size images and adds Chinese state headings using Pillow; no fake animation or implemented gameplay.
limitations: Independent text-to-image generations, not a reference-image-conditioned pair; framing, blade orientation and fine outfit details differ.
Compositional and coloured-ink direction samples, not game-ready split layers, calibrated sprites or an animation sequence.
No global theme switch or replacement of the already approved V6 assets was performed.
